title.narrative: CCJ-URT Legal support for land restitution 2017-2021
CCJ-URT Legal support for land restitution 2017-2021

description.narrative:
Colombianska juristkomissionen (CCJ) har ansökt till Sida om 23.3 miljoner SEK för att genomföra projektet ”Legal support for land restitution – CCJ 2017 – 2021” i Colombia under perioden 1 mars 2017 till 31 Mars 2021.
Projektets målsättning är att är att stödja säkerställandet av rättigheter för individer som utgör offer för fördrivning och påtvingat övergivande, och som har särskild legal representation i återlämnandeprocessen. CCJ kommer fortsätta ge juridisk representation i de 740 fallen baserat på ett strategiskt processinriktat förhållningssätt, samt stärka Myndigheten för markåterbördande (URT) samt akademiska institutioners kapacitet för de strategiska processerna genom erfarenheter och lärdomar.
Interventionens totala budget omfattar 24,4 miljoner SEK och finansieras till 75 % av Sverige. Återstående 25 % täcks för närvarande av USAID och förväntas även täckas av andra givare som EU, ILO och Colombias ombudsmannakontor. CCJ gemomför en fundraising-strategi för att täcka den totala budgeten.

The Colombian Commission of Jurist- CCJ has applied to Sida for funding of 23,3 million SEK to carry out the project “Legal support for land restitution – CCJ 2017- 2021” in Colombia during the period March 1, 2017 to March 31, 2021.
The project’s objective is to contribute to guarantee the rights of victims of land dispossession and forced abandonment with specialized legal representation in their land restitution processes. CCJ will continue the legal representation of the 740 cases based on a strategic litigation approach and strengthen the Unit for land restitution and Academia capacity for strategic litigation through experiences and lessons learned.
The intervention’s total budget is 24,4 million SEK and is 75% financed by Sweden.

This project was a second phase of the litigation strategy that started in 2014 with legal representation of victims of land grabbing. During the first phase and until December 2016, CCJ had legal representation of 1488 cases in 295 legal processes of which 58 have been resolved by judges rulings. This was the baseline for this second phase that started in March 2017 and went until April the 30th 2021. Up to December 2019, the CCJ represented 729 cases, grouped together in 61 legal separate processes. 536 were financed by Sweden in the four Departments of Bolivar, Cesar, Magdalena and Meta and 193 others were financed by USAID in the Departments of Antioquia, Cordoba, Cauca, Chocó and Putumayo. However, in the cases of Chimborazo and Bellacruz (Cesar) the number of represented people increased to 563 cases. These 563 cases, financed by Sweden, were grouped together in 40 separate legal processes and benefit 3061 people (including 1501 women). Up to May 2021, 20 of these processes have had a positive legal outcome, 7 are ready for a legal process, 3 had negative legal outcomes and the other 10 are still in the judicial phase.
In 2019, the Unit for land restitution requested the CCJ to return cases as this institution has been strengthened in recent years and therefore were able to receive such cases in fulfillment of its mandate. Hence, during 2020 and after consultation with victims, 163 cases that are covered by 23 separate legal processes were returned to the URT for their legal representation. These processes are dealt with by 5 territorial offices of the URT: 1 process with 2 cases in Chigorodó- Antioquia; 7 processes with 91 cases in Bolívar; 11 processes with 51 cases in Cesar; 1 process with 1 case in Meta and 3 processes with 18 cases in Magdalena. 13 of the 23 processes have already received positive legal decisions, 4 are ready to proceed with a legal process, 3 are still in the evidence phase and 3 have been allowed by the judge to start the judicial phase. Up to May 2021, the URT had formalized the authorization of 15 of the 23 processes and still need support by the CCJ to contact the victims of the 8 additional processes.
253 of the 563 cases did not want the URTs legal representation and then the victims requested CCJ to continue with the 14 legal processes. 10 processes are in Magdalena, 3 in Cesar and one in Bolivar. CCJ will continue this support with their own resources. This also shows the trust created between CCJ and the communities.
An external evaluation was developed between October and December 2019. The report concluded that the project has been very relevant and effective for victimss rights and to strengthen institutional capacities. The victims, the General prosecutors office, the Ombudsmans office, agrarian judges and magistrates, as well as some staff from regional offices at the Unit for land restitution, have recognized the important work done by CCJ in legal representation for victims, legal incidence before high courts, as well as in the psychosocial support and trust created with victims. The evaluators also concluded that CCJ has demonstrated strong capacity and commitment to develop this assignment.
